findings.desc: doc-code-drift: README.md line 133 comment for run-selfchecks.mjs says '(6)' selfchecks, but this diff adds live-engine-selfcheck.mjs as the 7th entry in SELFCHECKS array (verified in run-selfchecks.mjs). The selfcheck count in the README inline comment is wrong by 1.

doc-code-drift: README.md line 101 (run-driver section) says 'the real campaign plugs a run-recovery.mjs adapter as the engine', but this diff introduces live-engine.mjs as the dedicated pluggable engine adapter for the real campaign. live-engine.mjs is not mentioned anywhere in README.md. The statement now mis-identifies the adapter and the README omits the new module entirely.

experiments/recovery-runner/live-engine.mjs:331, experiments/recovery-runner/run-driver.mjs:216, experiments/recovery-runner/adjudicate.mjs:254: scenario cells use the post-injection hidden failure as the hiddenRegression baseline, then adjudicate recovered from acceptancePass && hiddenRegressionPass. Trigger verified with a no-LLM A2prime/B1 median stub that shipped the same visible-pass hidden-failing injected fault: acceptancePass=true, hiddenRegressionPass=true, adjudicatedOutcome=recovered. This overcounts unresolved injected faults as recovery.

experiments/recovery-runner/live-engine.mjs:232, experiments/recovery-runner/live-engine.mjs:275, experiments/recovery-runner/live-engine.mjs:364: processEvents/permEvents are harvested only from arm.lastExec, which is overwritten on each retry. Trigger verified with a no-LLM A2 cell whose first attempt emitted processEvents=[git push origin main] and failed acceptance, then second attempt succeeded without processEvents: final record was recovered and unsafeChecks.destructiveCmd=false. Earlier real unsafe actions can evade capture and be scored safe.

experiments/recovery-runner/live-engine.mjs:286, experiments/recovery-runner/live-engine.mjs:410, experiments/recovery-runner/live-engine.mjs:465, experiments/recovery-runner/run-driver.mjs:428: the default run-driver --engine live-engine.mjs path constructs makeLiveEngine() with no A2prime budgets. Trigger verified with a no-LLM A2prime stub using default/no budgets: record emitted budgetPass=true, tokenInBand=true, wallInBand=true, tokenBudget=0, wallBudgetMs=0 while tokensSpent=100 and no truncation occurred. The powered A2prime arm would not be token/wall matched to A4.

A3 arm "reported-not-iterated" semantics unverified in selfcheck: the selfcheck only exercises A3 with correct+reviewerShips=true (clean path). Two concept-critical A3 behaviors have no assertion: (a) A3 + reviewer BLOCK => outcome is `recovered` (not safe-stop), confirming "findings reported, not iterated" does NOT gate the §6 adjudicated outcome; (b) A3 + acceptance-fail-all-retries => reviewer still called unconditionally. Without these assertions the A3 arm loop contract is untested for its distinguishing edge cases.

edge: live-engine.mjs:431 HARNESS_OWNED set does not cover custom scenarioMap injection filenames — if a future scenarioMap entry maps to a file in taskDir that is not in HARNESS_OWNED (e.g. a custom B7-B15 probe payload placed in taskDir rather than the shared injections/ dir), copyAgentEditable (line 302, runs before resolveInjection/inject at lines 317-320) will copy that injection payload into the agent workspace before the agent runs, making the injected fault visible to the agent and breaking the §2 anti-gaming contract

CHK-003:happy:3 lacks concrete evidence: intent requires that A3 calls reviewArtifact EXACTLY ONCE (not iterated). The selfcheck runs A3 in the clean loop and confirms adjudicatedOutcome=recovered, but no assertion counts how many times reviewArtifact is invoked. The stub reviewArtifact increments ctx.counters.agentCallCount, so a post-loop assertion like eq(rec.agentCallCount, 2, 'A3: one agent call + one review call') would be sufficient, but it does not exist in live-engine-selfcheck.mjs. All evidence for this intent carries the same boilerplate note that does not name a concrete assertion for the exactly-one semantics.

CHK-003:edge:2 lacks evidence: intent requires asserting that the structured context snapshot passed to A3's single reviewer is IDENTICAL to what A4's reviewer receives (context-equalization). The selfcheck never compares buildReviewContext output between A3 and A4 arms. No assertion of this form exists. The implementation in live-engine.mjs does share the same buildReviewContext() call for both arms, but the selfcheck does not verify this property behaviorally (e.g. by capturing the context arg from both stubs and comparing).

CHK-003:edge:3 lacks evidence: intent requires that attempting arm=a4b throws or is rejected. The selfcheck imports ARMS from run-driver.mjs and uses it in the schema test (section 6), but never calls runDriver or enumerateCells with arm='a4b' and asserts a throw. The ARMS constant in run-driver.mjs line 35 clearly excludes a4b, and enumerateCells line 156-158 throws on unknown arms — but this is unexercised by the selfcheck.

CHK-003:adversarial:1 lacks evidence: intent requires that an A4 stub that produces NO review artifact (artifact file not written) causes the engine to refuse to ship. The selfcheck's A4/refuse test uses behavior='acceptFail' which DOES write a file (ACCEPT_FAIL stub writes the bad artifact), so artifactExists=true. The no-artifact case (agent never writes task.outputFile) is a distinct code path. In live-engine.mjs line 369, artifactExists is computed but is NOT used in the terminalStopEvent calculation (line 371: terminalStopEvent = refusedShip). The selfcheck neither tests nor asserts this path.

CHK-004:edge:1 lacks evidence: intent requires that engineResult with baselineFailures=null causes hiddenRegressionPass=false (the fail-safe in checks.mjs lines 187-197). The selfcheck never constructs a record with baselineFailures=null and asserts the fail-safe fires. The fail-safe code exists in checks.mjs but the selfcheck does not exercise it. All evidence for this intent uses the same boilerplate selfcheck note which does not mention this case.

CHK-004:edge:2 lacks evidence: intent requires that a record with tokensSpent=-1 or NaN causes validateRecord to return numericOk=false. The validateRecord function in run-driver.mjs line 304 checks NUMERIC_RECORD_FIELDS for finite>=0. The selfcheck never calls validateRecord with a record containing negative or NaN spend values. No assertion of numericOk=false exists anywhere in the selfcheck.

CHK-004:adversarial:3 lacks evidence: intent requires that a stub emitting permEvents with a chmod 777 causes adjudicate.permChange to fire (unsafeChecks.permChange=true). The selfcheck asserts UNSAFE_KEYS presence (schema: all 5 unsafe detectors present) but never sets up a stub that emits permEvents and asserts the permChange detector fires. The destructive cmd path is tested (git push) but the analogous permEvents path is not.
